title: Bubble up the order
prompt:
The starter reads a count and then that many values, in a tangle, into the word array `tangle`. Bubble sort them in place, smallest first; the print loop at the bottom will show whatever order the memory ends up in.

Bubble sort is two nested loops: the outer one counts passes, the inner one walks adjacent pairs, swapping any pair that is out of order. Both elements of a pair load with the scaled-index form, and a swap is storing them back in each other's slots. After each pass the largest remaining value has bubbled to the end, so the inner walk can shrink as the passes go by.

## what is checked

- the values, one per line, in ascending order
- the program exits cleanly
- the sort rearranges memory (`str` present, comparisons present)
- the same holds for other arrays you do not see: one value, already sorted, reversed, and repeats
starter:
// sort an array in place, then print it smallest first
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(base_r, x22)
define(i_r, w19)
define(j_r, w20)
define(n_r, w21)
define(a_r, w23)
define(b_r, w24)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_out:    .string "%d\n"

        .bss
        .balign 4
n_m:        .skip 4
tangle:     .skip 128                       // room for 32 words

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // how many values follow
        ldr     x1, =n_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =n_m
        ldr     n_r, [x9]
        ldr     base_r, =tangle
        mov     i_r, 0
        b       fill_test
fill_loop:
        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the next value into its slot
        add     x1, base_r, i_r, sxtw 2
        bl      scanf
        add     i_r, i_r, 1
fill_test:
        cmp     i_r, n_r
        b.lt    fill_loop

        // TODO: bubble sort. The outer loop runs n - 1 passes; the
        // inner loop walks adjacent pairs, loading both with the
        // scaled-index form, comparing, and storing them back swapped
        // whenever the left one is bigger.

        mov     i_r, 0
show_loop:
        cmp     i_r, n_r
        b.ge    finished
        ldr     a_r, [base_r, i_r, sxtw 2]
        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, a_r
        bl      printf
        add     i_r, i_r, 1
        b       show_loop
finished:

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
